facts.big: have already / Could you tell me…?
facts.label: Revisão do aeroporto
facts.sub: Misture present perfect (Have you checked in yet?), passado (Did you remember…?), modais (didn’t have to) e perguntas indiretas (Could you tell me where the gate is?).

facts.label: Já fiz
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio para algo recente ou sem hora marcada: Have you checked in yet? I have already found a cafe. Use already e yet; never aparece em I have never had such a long wait.

facts.label: Aconteceu
facts.sub: Use o passado quando o tempo está fechado: Did you remember your water bottle? I did. Depois de did e didn’t, use o verbo base: I didn’t have to pay.

compare.ask: Could you tell me where the gate is?
compare.br: No Brasil, perguntamos “o voo já saiu?” sem pensar no tempo verbal.
compare.tip: Diga: “Could you tell me where the gate is?”
compare.us: Em inglês, use o present perfect para algo recente: Have you checked in yet? Para um momento passado, use o passado: Did you remember? Para ser educado, use Could you tell me…?

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: Could you tell me where the gate is?
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Have you checked in yet? is a present perfect question.
We say “I have went to the gate.”
items.why: We say I have gone or I went.

items.s: Could you tell me why? is a polite question.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Have you checked in yet? is a present perfect question. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I have went to the gate.” → Falso (We say I have gone or I went.)
Could you tell me why? is a polite question. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A day at the airport · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a stormy morning at the airport in Houston. Hundreds of people walk with bags and tickets. Gabe has already arrived and he waits near the doors. His friend Eva comes in with a small bag. They have planned this trip for months. Now they must find out about their flight.

“Eva, have you checked in yet? The line for security is long.” says Gabe. “Yes, I have. I just got my boarding pass on my phone.” says Eva. “Good. Do you know which gate our flight leaves from?” says Gabe.
